rv.q: With memorable direction and songs full of joy and sincerity, it reinforces the fact that while it can be shite being Scottish, it can also be a real privilege to call this place home.
It’s a pleasingly surreal tale about loneliness and loss, in other words, in a society where apps like Tinder seem to offer 30-year-olds like Joy their only hope of ever not being alone.

cn.t: Critics praise this irreverent romp through Scottish history for its playful energy and whimsical storytelling, with the eccentric toilet narrator delivering both fun and sincerity in equal measure.
